title: Scale planner timeout when a revision round escalates effort
summary: Retry of job 20261114-041123-hvyh, whose planning stopped at round 2 (xhigh, 606 s, 600 s deadline). In planning_round, when the planner revision setting raises effort above the planner's own, the planner time limit is multiplied (2x, a constant) instead of staying at planner_timeout_s. The prior job's follow-up-queue feature is not part of this job.

defaults_applied.how: New unit tests plus cargo test and clippy criteria.
One focused change in the planning step.
Scales the limit with the escalation instead of just raising the base timeout.
Enforced in code and a test.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs planning_round (lines ~141-165) picks model/effort via jc.config.models.planner_revision_setting when round > 1 or mechanical_passes > 0, then passes cfg.planner_timeout_s to agent_spec; crates/athena-data/src/config.rs (planner_timeout_s at line 229, planner_revision_effort at 343, planner_revision_setting near 386, effort_rank) defines the setting; tests in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs (config helper near line 1328 writes planner_revision_effort and planner_timeout_s = 600). No record or data file is added, so check_record_file/AnyRecord are not involved. The timeout is measured directly on the AgentSpec built for the planner call.

Existing code: crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs and crates/athena-data/src/config.rs are extended; the existing planner_revision_setting result is reused to decide whether effort was escalated, and no new config key is added.

Design call: the scale is a fixed constant (2x, so 1200 s from the base 600 s) applied only when the revision effort differs from the planner's own effort; round 1, seeded first calls and unescalated revisions keep planner_timeout_s. A config key was avoided so athena.toml and defaults.toml stay unchanged; the 2x value is an estimate, based on 606 s observed against a 600 s limit.

Job 20261114-041123-hvyh left no candidate changes, so there is no work to keep or drop. Its original deliverables (followups.rs, steward.rs and others) are dropped from this job and remain unbuilt follow-up; that request will need to be retried separately.
Audience: Sri, who runs hard jobs and judges whether a stronger revision round can finish; the planner prompt is unchanged. Consumers: none found (no config deliverable).

acceptance_criteria.text: A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs configures planner_revision_effort higher than the planner's effort with planner_timeout_s = 600, runs a revision round (round 2), and asserts the planner AgentSpec timeout is greater than 600 s. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
A test asserts that round 1 and a revision without escalated effort (no planner_revision_effort set, or not stronger) still use exactly planner_timeout_s. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.

The diff in crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs scales cfg.planner_timeout_s only when the revision setting raises effort, via a named constant with a doc comment saying why (job 20261114-041123-hvyh hit 600 s at xhigh).
The deliverables are only planning.rs, run/tests.rs and CHANGELOG.md; athena.toml, defaults.toml, hestia.rs, the prompts and records/ are unchanged in the diff.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy and cargo test pass on the final tree (recorded Athena checks count).
CHANGELOG.md has an entry recording the planner time limit scaling and citing job 20261114-041123-hvyh.

out_of_scope: The follow-up queueing feature from job 20261114-041123-hvyh (followups.rs, steward.rs, manage.rs, reading.rs, lib.rs, crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs): dropped here, to be retried as its own request.
Backfilling lost follow-ups from job 20261114-034034-fgwz and the hestia.rs findings; hestia.rs unchanged.
A new athena.toml or defaults.toml key, changes to planner_timeout_s itself, critic timeout, planner prompts, workflows and records/.
departures: Slightly lower cost and time than the reference: a small change in one function, though hard planning adds a planner and critic.
urgent_reason: Cuts failed planning attempts: a revision round at xhigh timed out at 600 s and stopped job 20261114-041123-hvyh before any code was written.
hard_reason: Changes the run pipeline's planning step: the time limit that decides whether a planner round is stopped.
